title: client-disconnect-reconnect-handshake-cancel-safeguards-openai-compat
author: Asha Patel
description:
Motivation: Customers were seeing indeterminate behavior when clients disconnected mid-stream (mobile network flaps, proxy resets) and then reconnected: generated tokens could be duplicated or lost, function-calling side effects were inconsistently applied, and OpenAI-compat clients received confusing error payloads. This PR introduces a pragmatic, opt-in streaming lifecycle handshake and cancellation safeguards to make disconnect/reconnect/resume behavior deterministic and backwards-compatible.

Summary of changes: Adds a resume handshake token, server-side grace-window and per-stream timeout semantics, improved mapping for OpenAI-compat abort/cancel errors, and safe function-calling guarantees when clients reconnect. Includes runtime changes, adapter mapping, SDK surface notes, tests, and docs.

Design goals and constraints: 1) Backwards-compatible by default: existing clients continue working with current semantics; new handshake is enabled via header or query param. 2) Deterministic retries/resume: resumed streams should continue from the last acknowledged token, never re-execute completed function calls. 3) Minimal latency impact for non-resuming clients: default flow retains current fast-path. 4) Observable: metrics for resume attempts, aborted-inflight, and resume success rate.

Protocol and API changes (high level): - New optional outbound header: X-Resume-Token: client-supplied token used to correlate a resumed stream with a recent disconnected stream. Servers issue a Resume-Offer frame at disconnect that contains a server-side resume token and last-ack offset. - New request query param: resume_window_ms (default 30000) controls how long the server will honor resume attempts for a given stream id. - New server timeout param: stream_idle_timeout_ms (default 60000) to bound resource retention post-disconnect. - New SSE/Chunk frames: RESUME_OFFER, RESUME_ACCEPT, RESUME_REJECT, HEARTBEAT to coordinate state. (When using HTTP/2 gRPC-like streaming the frames are translated into control messages.)

Server behavior and safety: - On client disconnect, the runtime records the last-confirmed token offset and issues a RESUME_OFFER when it is safe to resume (i.e., KV cache intact). The offer includes a server_resume_token and last_ack_position. - The server holds execution state for resume_window_ms. If a new connection presents X-Resume-Token matching a live server_resume_token and offset <= last_ack_position + hysteresis, the server responds with RESUME_ACCEPT and resumes token emission from next position. - To avoid double-execution of function/tool calls, function-call side effects are only marked committed after the client acknowledges receipt of a special CALL_CONFIRM frame. During resume, the runtime consults the call ledger and will not re-run committed calls; in-flight calls that did not reach CALL_CONFIRM will be retried once with idempotency keys. - If the resume fails (mismatch token or expired window), the server returns RESUME_REJECT and the client may reopen a fresh stream; server enforces server-side backpressure and cold-start fallback to alternate model variants if capacity is constrained.

OpenAI compatibility adapter changes: - Map native abort/disconnect reasons to OpenAI-compat error semantics: aborted-by-client => code: 499/cancelled with message "Client cancelled stream"; server-timeout => 503 with body matching OpenAI shape. - For streaming-chat endpoints, the adapter now honors X-Resume-Token and includes resume metadata in the chunked response for OpenAI-compat clients that opt-in via header "X-OpenAI-Resume: 1". This preserves OpenAI-compatible behavior while enabling deterministic resume. - Function-calling: adapter uses the new CALL_CONFIRM frame to report that a function invocation payload has been delivered; only then will OpenAI-compatible /responses include function result committed state.

Compatibility and opt-in rollout: - Feature is guarded under feature flag streaming-lifecycle-v2. Default off for all existing accounts; enabled on canary accounts and progressively rolled to larger tenants. - SDKs (Python/TS) will include helpers to manage resume tokens and heartbeat handling. Docs include migration notes and an example for mobile reconnect patterns.

Testing and observability: - Unit + integration tests that simulate flapping connections, mid-call disconnects, duplicate resume attempts, and expired resume windows. - Added e2e tests for OpenAI-compat streaming in CI matrix. - New metrics: streaming.resume_attempts, streaming.resume_success, streaming.resume_rejections, streaming.inflight_call_retries. Added tracing spans for handshake phases: handshake.offer, handshake.accept, handshake.reject, handshake.timeout.

Migration checklist: - [x] Implement server-side resume token store and eviction. - [x] Add SDK helpers and docs. - [x] Add OpenAI-compat adapter mapping and tests. - [x] Add metrics and tracing. - [x] Canaries in prod and rollout automation.

Risks and mitigations: - Risk: state retention increases memory footprint on high-concurrency workloads. Mitigation: server enforces stream_idle_timeout_ms and per-tenant limits; resume_window_ms default is conservative. - Risk: tool/function idempotency edge cases. Mitigation: explicit CALL_CONFIRM semantics and idempotency keys; we test common patterns and add telemetry for uncommitted calls.

Rollout plan: Canary on 3 customers and internal staging for 48 hours; measure resume_success and in-flight_call_retries; open rollout gradually, disabling on SLO breach.

This description is intentionally dense; see changed files for implementation details and inline comments.
commits: a9b1f7a: runtime: add resume token store and expiry logic
b2c3e5d: runtime: emit RESUME_OFFER/HEARTBEAT control frames and record last_ack_position
c3d4f6e: adapter/openai: honor X-Resume-Token and map abort reasons to OpenAI-compatible errors
d4e5f7b: sdk/python: expose ResumeToken helper and heartbeat client example
e5f6a8c: docs: streaming lifecycle handshake design doc and migration guide
review_comments: Tomás Nguyen: Overall approach looks good. A few clarifying questions: 1) How do we prevent resume tokens from being reused by malicious clients? 2) Can we tighten the default resume_window_ms for free-tier tenants?

Asha Patel: Answers: 1) Resume tokens are cryptographically signed and bound to tenant+stream id; we also rotate and revoke tokens on explicit stream termination. 2) Yes, we added per-tenant overrides and free-tier defaults to 15s to limit retention (see runtime/streaming/handshake.go).
Maya Reddy: We need more unit tests around function-call idempotency when network fails between CALL_CONFIRM and ACK. Also please add a metric for uncommitted_call_retries.
Asha Patel: Added tests in handshake_test.go and adapter tests; added streaming.uncommitted_call_retries metric. Also added explicit lint justification for the new control frame names.
Ben Carlson: CI flakes on the OpenAI-compat e2e in the first run, re-ran and it passed. Approving once CI is green.
merge_outcome: Merged by squash into main on 2025-11-19 (squash-merge). Merge commit message: 'streaming: add optional resume handshake and cancellation safeguards (ENG-2642)'.
release_notes: Optional streaming resume handshake: opt-in via X-Resume-Token or resume_window_ms. Improves determinism for reconnects and adds safer function-call semantics during reconnects. Backwards compatible by default. See docs/streaming-lifecycle-handshake.md for migration steps.
notes: Feature gated under streaming-lifecycle-v2. Operational runbook added to /docs/oncall/streaming-handshake.md.
